job.title: National Sales Manager - Australia
job.description:
The Company
Our client operates in the Australian crop protection market, working with distributors, agronomists, advisers and growers to connect its product portfolio with the needs of Australian farming systems. Its commercial approach brings together national sales coverage, strategic customer partnerships and collaboration across marketing, technical, regulatory and supply chain functions.
  
With a focus on profitable growth and customer outcomes, the business is seeking a National Sales Manager to translate commercial priorities into practical sales execution, strengthen channel relationships and develop the capability of its geographically dispersed Australian sales team.
  
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Country Head, you will be hands on yet lead Australian sales strategy and execution, with a team of twelve. This national leadership role combines distributor and strategic account management with team development, portfolio execution and commercial planning, connecting business priorities with customer needs to deliver sustainable revenue growth and profitability.
  
With some exciting new active ingredients and product launches in the future, this is a role you can make your own and grow its market position. You will take ownership of the national sales plans, budgets and forecasts and lead significant customer negotiations while guiding new product launches. Working across commercial and technical functions, you will turn market intelligence into clear priorities, strengthen account planning and align sales activity with demand and supply requirements.
  
About You
To be successful in this position, we are seeking the following:
  • Significant commercial sales experience in Australian agriculture, crop protection, agricultural inputs or a closely related market.
  • Demonstrated hands on experience leading, coaching and developing geographically dispersed sales teams.
  • Strong retail distributor relationships and experience managing strategic customers, national accounts and commercial negotiations.
  • Commercial acumen across sales strategy, pricing, margin management, budgeting and forecasting.
  • Credible knowledge of Australian cropping systems and the ability to connect product positioning with customer and grower needs.
  • A collaborative, accountable approach, with strong cross-functional communication skills and willingness to travel nationally. Qualifications in agriculture, agribusiness or business are desirable.
Why This Role
Take ownership of national sales strategy while remaining close to customers and Australian agriculture. With nine direct reports and access to the Country Head, you can shape commercial priorities, make this job your own and develop team capability and influence product launches, channel partnerships and business growth.
  
For a confidential conversation please call David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply with a cover letter addressing the advertisement criteria and a current resume.

job.title: Lead Production Agronomist
job.description:
The Company
GenTech Seeds is a recognised premium brand in Australian agribusiness and the exclusive producer and distributor of Pioneer® brand products in Australia.

The business works closely with growers to produce hybrid seed products suited to Australian farming systems, with a major seed manufacturing and distribution site based at Narromine in Central West NSW. The Narromine site brings together production, quality, field operations and distribution within a highly seasonal seed production environment.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Site Manager, this role will lead technical agronomy across commercial seed production in the Macquarie Valley.

The role is focused on corn through summer and canola through winter, with some involvement in sorghum, production trials and broader improvement projects. It combines crop agronomy, grower engagement and close collaboration with production, field and quality teams.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Manage seasonal agronomy programs across corn, canola and sorghum seed production.
  • Support growers with crop establishment, nutrition, irrigation, pest and disease decisions.
  • Monitor crop performance, seasonal risk, yield potential and seed quality requirements.
  • Contribute to production planning, trials and continuous improvement projects.
Seed production experience would be valuable, but the business is open to experienced agronomists from broader broadacre, row crop or production backgrounds who can bring technical depth, sound judgement and the right team approach.

About You
You are a practical agronomist who enjoys being close to the crop, the grower and the commercial outcome.

Experience in corn, canola or seed production would be valuable, although sound crop agronomy, good judgement and grower communication will be the key.

You will bring:
  • Agronomy experience across broadacre, irrigated or seed production systems.
  • Confidence working directly with growers, contractors and operational teams.
  • Sound judgement across crop performance, timing, quality and seasonal risk.
  • A hands-on, accountable approach with the ability to take ownership of a region.
Why This Role?
This is a genuine opportunity to step into a senior agronomy role with clear ownership of a key production region. You will be close to the decisions that affect crop performance, seed quality and grower outcomes, while working within a respected national business with strong systems, established grower relationships and a premium brand in the market.

For someone who enjoys technical agronomy, commercial production and building trust with growers, this role offers the chance to have real influence across a high-value seed production program.

How to Apply
For a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha Lima on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Farm Advisory Specialist
job.description:
The Company
Founded in Sweden in 1883, DeLaval has supported dairy farmers for more than 140 years and is today a leading global supplier of dairy farming solutions. Its offering spans the full dairy operation – from automatic milking through the DeLaval VMS™ portfolio and conventional parlours, to feeding, housing, animal health, milk cooling and digital herd management – all designed to work together to improve farm performance. Guided by its vision to make sustainable food production possible, DeLaval helps farmers lift productivity and profitability while safeguarding animal welfare, and supports Australian dairy farmers through a strong network of Dealers and specialist teams.

The Opportunity
An exciting opportunity has become available for a Farm Advisory Specialist to join the DeLaval Oceania Technical team. Reporting to the Technical Support Manager, you will provide specialist farm advisory, milking performance and technology support that adds measurable value to dairy farmers, while strengthening DeLaval's Dealer and customer capability.

Working closely with farmers, Dealers and the Sales, Technical and Project teams, you will support customers from project concept through to commissioning, training and ongoing farm optimisation.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing specialist farm advisory and milking performance support across Automated Milking Systems (AMS) and Conventional Milking Systems (CMS)
  • Assessing farm, herd and system performance and delivering practical, data-driven recommendations to improve efficiency, animal welfare and profitability
  • Acting as a specialist in DelPro, herd management and Digital Services, helping customers use system data to make better decisions
  • Supporting projects from solution design through installation, commissioning, handover and end-user training
  • Building strong customer and stakeholder relationships while upholding the DeLaval brand and a strong safety culture
This is a national, field-based role with regular travel to customer farms, Dealer locations and project sites across Australia, including regional dairy areas, with occasional international travel for DeLaval training and development.

About You
You will be a customer-focused dairy professional who enjoys translating data and technology into practical results on farm. To be successful, you will bring:
  • Several years experience in a technical, sales, farm advisory or related dairy industry role (including on farm experience)
  • Knowledge of AMS and CMS milking system operation, performance and service
  • A strong understanding of dairy herd management, farm performance KPIs and farming practices
  • Experience with DelPro or other herd management software would be advantageous
  • Strong coaching, training and communication skills, with the ability to build relationships with farmers and Dealers
  • Commercial awareness, strong data interpretation and problem-solving skills
Why This Role
This is a great opportunity to join a globally recognised brand and make a real difference to the performance of Australian dairy farms.

To apply, please click APPLY and submit your resume and cover letter. For a confidential discussion, please contact Ryan Hoiberg at Rimfire Resources on 1300 380 701.

job.title: Executive Assistant to the Managing Director
job.description:

The Cotton Research and Development Corporation (CRDC) delivers research, development and extension outcomes for Australia’s cotton industry. A partnership between the Commonwealth Government and cotton growers, CRDC invests in world-leading innovation and transformative technologies that benefit growers, the wider industry and regional communities.
  
Working closely with growers, researchers and innovators, CRDC is ambitious, agile and adaptive, with a strong focus on impact, accountability and continuous improvement.
  
CRDC offers an exceptional working environment, a genuine passion for the cotton sector and a strong organisational purpose.

The Opportunity
This position reports directly, and works closely with, the Managing Director (MD) in all matters of support.  You will provide a wide variety of assistance to the MD, with primary responsibility to maximise the opportunity cost of their time by being ‘one step ahead’.  Trust with the MD is vital.

Responsibilities include managing priorities, commitments, correspondence, stakeholder relationships, briefing materials, travel and executive workflows to maximise leadership effectiveness and organisational impact.
  
Furthermore, duties include:

  • Think ahead and anticipate solutions in advance
  • Schedule and coordinate MD and executive meetings and take minutes
  • Coordinate international and domestic travel arrangements for MD and general support to the CRDC team as required
  • Work closely with MD and at all times remain discreet and professional
About You
To be successful in this role you will need to be based in Narrabri and have:
  • 5+ years’ experience in an EA role
  • Have a reputation for being discreet, trustworthy, and able to work closely with an executive, yet remain a positive team player across the business
  • You are highly organised with excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Excellent attention to detail and used to ‘managing up’.
  • You have prior experience working well across all levels of internal management and staff, as well as external stakeholders
  • You are highly ethical, discreet, and understand the importance of confidentiality
  • As expected, you will have advanced level in Microsoft Office, excellent internet research skills, and be highly skilled at systems, processes, structure
  • Ability to prioritize, manage and meet multiple deadlines
  • Relevant qualifications will be highly regarded
This is a great position, working for a professional and supportive MD, who will value your contribution. A positive work culture with a genuine purpose. An attractive salary is on offer befitting the role and your experience.  CRDC has a team of over 30 and plays a key role in the cotton sector.
 
Please apply with your cover letter and fresh resume, or don’t hesitate to call David Jackson on 1300 380 701

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a premier, large-scale horticultural business with extensive operations spanning across farming, state of the art packing facilities, cold storage, and a multi-channel domestic and export distribution network. Operating across a national multi-season footprint, the business is dedicated to operational excellence, sustainable produce supply and continuous growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, this high-impact Finance Business Partner position is based in Central Queensland. The role provides strategic financial leadership, deep analytical insight, and commercial guidance to operational teams across the company’s premier assets and grower networks in Queensland.

You will partner with farm leaders, production teams and commercial executives, translating financial reporting into practical operational insight. Your advice will support decisions that improve profitability, control costs and prioritise capital investment.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Developing detailed block, variety, and planting-age profitability models—tracking growing, harvest, and post-harvest costs per hectare, tonne, and bin across all planted areas.
  • Evaluating sub-breakeven blocks and building comprehensive financial business cases for orchard removal, replanting or retention strategies.
  • Governing capitalised operating expenditure boundaries, immature block schedules, and biological asset/inventory reconciliations to ensure clear visibility between accounting and cash flow impacts.
  • Managing unit-level labour productivity metrics and operational input costs to drive cost convergence across properties.
  • Owning annual budgets, rolling operational forecasts, seasonal working capital models, and capital expenditure tracking across peak harvest windows.
  • Overseeing standalone profit and loss, grower settlement models, and marketing margin allocations under exclusive commercial variety licenses
  • Managing cost-to-serve analysis by sales channel, maintaining license compliance registers, modelling program working capital and assessing counterparty exposure across grower bases.
  • Leading month-end close procedures, entity financial reporting, tax/grant compliance, and external audit support while embedding robust cost-coding discipline.
About You
The ideal candidate will be a commercially astute, CA or CPA qualified finance professional who can translate complex financial information into clear, practical insights for operational leaders.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification with a relevant degree in Accounting, Finance, or Economics.
  • At least five years’ experience, including a minimum of two years in a business partnering role within agricultural, horticultural, food manufacturing or FMCG setting.
  • Proven experience in grower pools, supplier settlement, consignment accounting, or commercial licence and royalty frameworks will be highly regarded.
  • Advanced financial modelling capabilities with the ability to independently build robust 5-year business cases and capital proposals.
  • Demonstrated track record of identifying, quantifying, and delivering cost reduction initiatives, with measurable impact on financial performance.
  • Strong proficiency with Excel, modern ERP/finance systems and business intelligence tools (Power BI, Tableau).
  • Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to constructively challenge operational managers and build collaborative relationships.
Why This Role
This high-visibility role offers direct access to senior leaders and meaningful influence over operational strategy, asset development and value creation across a growing horticultural business. It is an opportunity to combine commercial finance expertise with hands-on operational partnering in a complex, multi-site environment.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701. To apply, visit www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Laboratory Technician
job.description:
The Company
Searles is a long-established Australian horticultural business producing composts, potting mixes and growing media used by customers across the country.

Part of a larger group, the business combines deep product knowledge with practical manufacturing capability and a strong commitment to quality. The Kilcoy site offers a supportive working environment where testing, production and product performance are closely connected.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Technical Manager, you will help maintain product quality across the Kilcoy operation.

The role combines routine laboratory testing with practical work across the production site. You will monitor composting and finished products, complete batch release checks, maintain accurate records and communicate results with operators.

Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Conducting routine testing on composts and finished products
  • Monitoring temperature, pH and EC across production processes
  • Completing batch release checks against specifications
  • Communicating results and required adjustments to operators
  • Supporting product trials, sample management and external testing
 
You will take ownership of a regular testing schedule and organise your priorities across the week. The work is structured and process-driven, with a mix of laboratory and outdoor activity.

The role is based at the Kilcoy site, accessible from Caboolture, Morayfield, Esk, Fernvale and Toogoolawah.

About You
You are reliable, methodical and take pride in producing accurate work.

Laboratory experience would be useful, although Searles is open to candidates from quality, manufacturing, agriculture, horticulture, environmental science or related backgrounds. Training can be provided to someone with a sound technical mindset and a consistent approach.

To succeed, you will bring:
  • Strong attention to detail and accurate record keeping
  • A practical, technically minded approach
  • The ability to manage routine priorities independently
  • Clear communication skills and confidence working with operational teams
  • Comfort working across laboratory and outdoor production environments
A qualification or experience in science, environmental science, agriculture, horticulture or a related area would be advantageous but is not essential.

Why this Role?
This is a practical opportunity to build laboratory and quality experience within a well-established horticultural business. You will take ownership of routine testing, contribute directly to product quality and receive support from an experienced Technical Manager.

Other benefits include:
  • Birthday day off in addition to annual leave
  • Access to garden products at wholesale prices
  • Flexible start and finish times aligned with production requirements
For more information or a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha-Lima at 1300 380 701 or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: HR Operations Manager
job.description:
Working within a highly successful, down-to-earth agricultural business, you’ll take responsibility for the day-to-day delivery of HR operations while continuing to improve the systems, processes and disciplines that support the business.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to sit on the side-lines and provide HR theory. We’re looking for someone who is comfortable rolling up their sleeves, working through issues with managers and employees, and making sure things actually happen.

You’ll need to be strong on process, compliance and attention to detail, but equally strong with people. The environment is straightforward and relatively informal, so your ability to build trust, communicate clearly and deal with people in a genuine and practical way will be critical.

The role
Working closely with managers across the business and the leadership team, you’ll oversee the delivery of core HR activities including:
  • Day-to-day HR operations and employee support
  • Employee relations and performance matters
  • Employment contracts, policies and documentation
  • HR systems, records and reporting
  • Recruitment, onboarding and offboarding
  • Remuneration and employment conditions
  • HR compliance and employment-related requirements
  • Improving HR processes and making them simpler and more consistent
  • Supporting managers to deal confidently with people matters
  • Ensuring HR initiatives are followed through and delivered
There will be plenty to manage, but also the opportunity to improve how things are done. You’ll need to be comfortable moving between the detail and the bigger picture, whether that means working through an employee issue, improving a process, checking documentation or helping a manager navigate a difficult conversation.

About you
We’re looking for someone who has solid HR experience but doesn’t need a highly structured corporate environment around them.
You’ll ideally be:
  • Hands-on and delivery focused with a strong bias towards action
  • Organised, methodical and good at following things through
  • Strong on HR process, governance and compliance
  • Commercial and pragmatic in the way you approach HR
  • Approachable and capable of building relationships across all levels
  • A clear, straightforward communicator who doesn't hide behind HR jargon
  • Comfortable working with both managers and frontline employees
  • Confident dealing with sensitive or challenging people matters
  • Able to bring structure and discipline without making things unnecessarily bureaucratic
  • Comfortable working independently and using good judgement
Experience within agriculture, agribusiness, food production, manufacturing, transport, resources or another operationally focused industry would be well regarded. More important, though, is that you understand how to work with practical, busy people and can adapt your approach accordingly.

The opportunity
This role will suit someone who enjoys travel, being close to the business and close to the people.

You won’t be expected to turn the organisation into a highly corporate HR environment. Instead, the focus is on making sure the fundamentals are right, managers are well supported, employees are treated fairly and consistently, and HR delivers what it says it will deliver.

If you’re an experienced HR professional who combines good process and compliance disciplines with common sense, energy and a genuine way with people, we’d like to hear from you. Please call Mark Turner or Mick Hay on 1300 380 701 for further information or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:

Our client is a leading horticultural business with large-scale farming operations, state-of-the-art packing facilities, cold storage, and a diversified domestic and export distribution network. With a national, multi-season footprint, the business is committed to operational excellence, a sustainable produce supply and continued growth.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, this high-impact Finance Business Partner position is based in Mooroopna, Victoria, and supports key horticultural operations across the Goulburn Valley and Riverina regions. It provides strategic financial leadership, commercial insight and operational partnering to farm management and senior leaders, with a focus on financial performance, capital investment and operational efficiency across several horticultural businesses.

You will work closely with operational leaders, translating complex financial data into practical commercial insights that support decision-making, improve profitability and strengthen financial accountability across the business.

  • At least five years' post-qualification experience, including at least two years in a finance business partnering role within a business operating across multiple sites.

This commercial finance position offers direct access to senior leadership and the opportunity to shape strategic and operational decisions across a large-scale agribusiness. job.title: Sales Agronomist
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established agricultural business supplying high-quality products, technical expertise and practical support to farmers, rural retailers and industry partners across Australia. With a strong commitment to research, innovation and customer outcomes, the business offers an extensive portfolio of proven products supported by an active pipeline of new solutions. A collaborative culture, respected market presence and commitment to sustainable agricultural productivity underpin its continued growth.

The Role
This autonomous, field-based position will be responsible for managing an established, and further developing, an important Southern Queensland territory. The region offers flexibility around location and may suit candidates based across the Darling Downs, Toowoomba, Brisbane, the Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Fraser Coast or surrounding agricultural areas.

You will build trusted relationships with rural retailers, producers, agronomists, consultants and industry groups, combining agronomic support with disciplined territory and business development. Working with an established portfolio and new product pipeline, you will identify the right product fit for local farming systems, support customers with practical technical advice and create sustainable commercial growth.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Developing and executing territory plans to achieve sales, margin and growth objectives
  • Managing and expanding relationships with existing customers while identifying new business opportunities
  • Providing practical agronomic, product and farm-system support to retailers, advisers and producers
  • Positioning existing and new products within local pasture, forage and mixed farming systems
  • Coordinating field demonstrations, retailer training, industry events and other promotional activities
  • Monitoring seasonal conditions, customer needs, competitor activity and market opportunities
  • Maintaining effective territory planning, customer records, reporting and market intelligence
  • Collaborating with technical, sales and marketing colleagues to deliver strong customer outcomes

This opportunity will suit a commercially minded agricultural professional who enjoys working with customers, translating technical information into practical recommendations and taking ownership of a territory. You may already be working in agronomy, agricultural sales, rural retail, farm advisory, account management, product development or a related customer-facing role.

Experience across pasture, forage, seed, livestock production, cropping or broader farm inputs would be valuable, but candidates with strong transferable agricultural knowledge and the ability to build credibility with producers and channel partners are encouraged to apply. Formal qualifications in agriculture, agronomy, science or business will be well regarded but are not essential where supported by relevant industry experience.

You will bring:
  • A sound understanding of agriculture and the ability to learn and communicate technical product information
  • Strong relationship-building, communication and influencing skills
  • A proactive, organised and commercially focused approach
  • The confidence to work independently while contributing to a geographically dispersed team
  • Good territory planning, time management and follow-through
  • A willingness to travel regularly throughout Southern Queensland
  • Current Australian work rights and a valid driver’s licence

This is an opportunity to take ownership of an established and strategically important territory with the backing of a respected agricultural business, a strong product portfolio and experienced technical and commercial colleagues.

A competitive salary package will be offered, including a fully maintained vehicle, phone and laptop, together with flexibility around where you are based within the region.

To discuss this opportunity confidentially, please contact Ryan Hoiberg at Rimfire Resources on 1300 380 701, or apply with your current resume and a brief outline of your relevant experience.

job.title: Territory Sales Manager - Great Southern Region
job.description:

As a Yates family-owned company operating in Australia for more than forty years, Pioneer Seeds believes they have a unique opportunity to help improve growers' operations and advance the science of agriculture in Australia. They do this by delivering improved seed genetics to farmers, developing and distributing high-quality corn, sorghum, canola, summer forage seed and inoculant products.

They believe that supporting their customers drive for success, means delivering farmers with the very best performing products on the market. They are committed to sharing their knowledge and passion for field agronomy through their dedicated people. The company is committed to comprehensive pre-and post-sales technical service, together with broader farm management advice and support.

The Position:

GenTech Seeds is wishing to appoint a Territory Sales Manager to develop and maintain close commercial relationships with resellers, influencers and canola producers. As a key member of the WA client facing team and reporting to the Regional Sales Manager, the Territory Sales Manager will focus on:
  • Actively promoting, recommending and selling Pioneer products
  • Connecting with the farmer network and ensuring all customer activity is correctly tracked
  • Working with resellers across the territory to develop, monitor and implement business plans and forecasting reports
  • Representing the business and brand at relevant industry functions and field days
  • Working closely with management, internal Canola Specialist and the WA team, to ensure that activity is aligned across the group.
The Person:

To be considered for this career defining opportunity, candidates will ideally possess the following:
  • Demonstrated sales experience within the agricultural industry
  • Experience working in territory management

job.title: Maintenance & Engineering Manager

Key areas of focus will include maintenance planning and scheduling, reliability and asset management, shutdown execution, capital and maintenance projects, contractor management, engineering governance, budgets and cost control, critical spares, CMMS improvement and the continued development of the maintenance team.

job.title: Farm Services Consultant
job.description:

They are committed to sharing their knowledge and passion for field agronomy through their dedicated people. The company is committed to comprehensive pre-and post-sales technical service, together with broader farm management advice and support.

This is a relationship-focused position designed to increase engagement with growers across the Central Wheatbelt, Lakes and Upper Great Southern. Working closely with both growers (80%) and reseller partners (20%), you will become a trusted local contact, providing product support, identifying opportunities and helping drive adoption of market-leading seed technologies.

  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with growers across the territory
  • Support product promotion, demonstrations and commercial trial activities
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities within the region

  • Assist with market intelligence gathering and territory development initiatives

job.title: Head of Innovation & Business Development

Our work includes national genetic evaluation and genomic services, industry data infrastructure, decision-support tools and software services designed to improve the productivity, profitability and sustainability of Australian dairy businesses.

DataGene is entering an exciting period of growth and evolution, with opportunities to increase adoption of its existing services, develop new data-driven products and build commercial and strategic partnerships across the dairy industry.

Many of DataGene's customers are reached through intermediary organisations—including genetics businesses, herd-testing organisations, veterinarians, consultants and industry advisors—so experience building effective partnerships and driving growth through indirect channels will be particularly valuable.

You will also lead a small team spanning stakeholder engagement, communications and product management, and work closely with DataGene's science and technology teams to translate customer and market needs into clear priorities.

You do not need to be a geneticist or herd-improvement specialist. We are looking for someone who understands the Australian dairy industry, is curious about technology and data, and has the commercial judgement and leadership capability to identify opportunities and turn them into outcomes.

The Person:

To be successful in this demanding but highly rewarding role, you will possess the following key skills and background:

Essential:
  • Demonstrated experience in business development including identifying and progressing growth opportunities, partnerships and/or new product offerings through indirect channels
  • Strong commercial acumen and proven experience developing business cases and assessing strategic fit, value and feasibility of new opportunities
  • Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to build and develop capability in others
  • Demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence with senior external stakeholders and represent an organisation effectively in industry settings
  • Experience in developing, delivering or selling data-driven or technology-enabled products and services
  • Experience translating customer and market insight into product requirements and priorities
  • Strong understanding of how to drive adoption, customer value and measurable uptake beyond stakeholder engagement alone
  • Ability to operate at both strategic and operational levels in a player-coach capacity
  • Strong knowledge of the dairy value chain (producer through to processor and retail)
Highly Desirable:
  • Established dairy industry relationships
  • Experience working with veterinarians, consultants, advisors or agricultural intermediaries
  • Experience building or leading product management functions
This is an outstanding newly created opportunity to play a key role in assisting in the evolution of DataGene’s genetics and breeding technologies and farm data strategy.

If you have a genuine passion for business development, ideally with exposure to the Australian Dairy, then in the first instance, please call Mick Hay or David Jackson on 1300 380 701 for an initial discussion or further information. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Regional Manager - Crop Research
job.description:

job.title: Territory Manager & Product Development Manager - Central Queensland
job.description:
The Company
Terranova Seeds is a specialist vegetable seeds company with more than 40 years’ experience. They supply commercial growers across Australia and New Zealand with a wide range of vegetable varieties and technical support. The business also exports selected products to the USA, SE Asia, PNG, the Pacific Islands, and customers in Europe, Africa, and Central America.
  
Partnering with leading international breeding companies, Terranova Seeds has grown consistently and become a market leader. With experienced technical staff, they provide high‑quality seed solutions trialled under local conditions to ensure reliability. The company is known for exceptional service, strong client relationships, and ongoing growth both locally and globally. Quality of product is their mantra.

The Opportunity  
Reporting to the National Sales Manager, this is a unique role that does not come along often. A hybrid function combining your sales and client management skills with product development responsibilities.
  
Your product development function will focus on the ongoing development of new products in the wider Queensland, gathering robust trial data forecasting and maintaining supplier relationships for existing and potential new commercial lines. You will do this by working closely with the National Product Development Manager, overseeing product development across the region as required while being highly connected to the end user, suppliers and client base in the supply of specific vegetable seed products. Focusing on crops such as tomatoes, peppers, cucurbits, green bean and sweetcorn. Overall, you are pivotal to delivering the desired products to an established and loyal client base while building a pipeline of products to introduce to growers in the future.  
  
Your sales focus is about business development. You will be to grow and develop revenue and gross profit within the region by sourcing and driving sales opportunities within the existing client base, while targeting new business clients for Terranova. Your selling skills and ability to influence and convert sales is vital for this role.   
  
You will:
  • Grow sales, volume and gross profit in the region to targets
  • Be present in the region looking for growth opportunities with existing and new clients
  • Spend the majority of your time client engaged developing sales and product development
  • Oversee ongoing trialling, development and launch of new vegetable varieties
  • Gather and report quality trial data to support new varieties (so you will be hands on)
  • Work closely with the product development team and sales team nationally to forecast sales, supply and inventory needs
About you

To be successful in this role you will ideally have:
  • Proven sales skills and experience in a similar environment
  • Technical experience in the vegetable seed industry and a sound knowledge of agronomy
  • Direct experience in running ongoing vegetable trial programs and reporting outcomes
  • Strong report writing skills with accuracy/attention to detail supported by exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • A natural ability and experience to listen and work positively with clients, suppliers, and growers
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications
Terranova offer a positive work culture where you will be provided with generous salary package including base, superannuation, car, phone, laptop and participate in the Company’s bonus plans. You will be expected to undertake local and international travel.

This is a unique opportunity with Terranova; an agile specialist vegetable seeds company which delivers tailored and ethical service delivery to its clients. A place where you have the flexibility to make decisions and lead by example yet work in a team environment.
   
For a confidential conversation please call David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply with a cover letter addressing the advertisement criteria and a fresh resume.

job.title: Quality Manager
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leading, large-scale horticultural business with integrated operations across farming, advanced packing facilities, cold storage, and domestic and export distribution. With a diverse multi-season operating footprint, the business is focused on operational excellence, sustainable produce supply, and continued growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the General Manager of Supply Chain, this newly created leadership position is based in Northern Victoria and plays a pivotal role in providing independent oversight of quality standards and quality assurance systems across the organisation’s national horticultural operations.

Covering multiple categories and production regions, the Quality Manager will own the quality framework from farm through to customer delivery, ensuring consistency in assessment standards, grading accuracy, food safety compliance, and quality data integrity. This role will operate across all stages of the value chain, including farming, harvest, cold storage, packing, dispatch, and third-party grower programs.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Owning and maintaining quality specifications, grading standards, assessment methodologies, and defect classification frameworks across commodities, varieties, customers, and markets.
  • Establishing and governing a consistent quality assurance system across multiple growing, storage and packing operations, ensuring reliable and defensible quality outcomes.
  • Defining and auditing quality controls throughout harvest, transport, cold storage, pre-sizing, packing, and dispatch operations.
  • Developing robust quality-loss attribution processes that accurately track grade movement and identify root causes throughout the supply chain.
  • Managing third-party grower assessment programs, dispute resolution processes, and quality compliance requirements.
  • Overseeing food safety, certification, market access compliance, customer claims investigations, corrective action programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Building quality assurance reporting and data governance frameworks that provide meaningful operational insights and support commercial and supply chain decision making.
About You
The successful candidate will be a technically strong and highly credible quality professional who combines scientific rigour, operational experience, and commercial awareness. You will be comfortable influencing stakeholders at all levels and capable of making independent decisions in situations where competing priorities exist.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • A tertiary qualification in Food Science, Food Technology, Horticulture, Agricultural Science, or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of eight years' experience in quality assurance or quality management within fresh produce, horticulture, food manufacturing, or other quality-sensitive production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing quality systems across multiple sites, products or operational locations.
  • Strong expertise in specification management, grading standards, defect classification, food safety systems and quality auditing.
  • Experience working with external certification bodies, regulatory frameworks and customer quality requirements.
  • Proven capability designing and delivering competency-based quality training programs within operational environments.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills, with the ability to interpret quality data, identify trends, and support evidence-based decision making.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence and drive compliance outcomes without direct reporting authority.
  • The flexibility and willingness to travel regularly across multiple growing and packing locations within Australia.
Why This Role
This is a unique opportunity to establish and lead a best-practice quality function within one of Australia's agriculture businesses.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701. Applications can be submitted via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Technical Product Development Manager - Home Pest
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established consumer products business with a strong presence across Australia and a portfolio of well-recognised brands sold through major retail channels.

With an established R&D and innovation capability, the business is investing in their home pest portfolio as part of its continued growth.  

The Opportunity
Reporting to the R&D Director and working closely across Marketing, Innovation, Supply Chain and Procurement, you will lead the technical development and commercialisation of the home pest portfolio.

Working predominantly through third-party formulation, testing, regulatory and manufacturing partners, you will determine the best technical pathway from product brief through to commercial launch.

There is genuine autonomy. You will bring the specialist knowledge and commercial judgement to recommend the right path, challenge proposals where required and keep multiple product developments moving.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading technical development from brief through to commercial launch
  • Evaluating formulations, efficacy, claims, stability and packaging compatibility
  • Selecting and managing external technical and manufacturing partners
  • Managing APVMA registration pathways and regulatory requirements
  • Driving projects through stage-gate and NPD processes
  • Managing technical risk against cost, timing and commercial requirements
  • Building internal technical knowledge to support the portfolio longer term
The role is offered as an 18-24 month fixed-term contract. Sydney is preferred, with Melbourne, Queensland and other East Coast locations considered for the right person. Travel to suppliers, manufacturers, laboratories and trial sites will be required.
  
About You
You are an experienced technical or product development professional who understands how to move regulated products from concept through to commercial launch.

Ideally, you will have worked within FMCG or a fast-paced consumer products environment, with an understanding of stage-gate development, commercial deadlines and the balance between technical and commercial requirements.

Direct consumer or household pest experience would be highly regarded. Candidates from professional pest control, crop protection or related chemical sectors will also be considered where they bring strong product commercialisation experience.

To succeed, you will bring:
  • 5+ years' experience within pest control or a closely related sector
  • Experience developing and commercialising regulated products
  • FMCG, consumer products or comparable NPD experience
  • Knowledge of insecticides, rodenticides and pest-control technologies
  • Working knowledge of APVMA requirements and registration pathways
  • Experience managing external manufacturers and technical partners
  • Strong project management, commercial judgement and communication skills
A tertiary qualification in entomology, chemistry, formulation science, biological science or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

Why This Role?
This is a rare opportunity to become the technical specialist behind a new product category within an established consumer business. You’ll have the scope to influence the technical direction, manage the right external partners and see a portfolio move from concept through to products in market.

For someone who knows the pest-control market and enjoys the pace of product commercialisation, there is plenty here to get hold of.

For more information or a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha-Lima on 1300 380 701 or apply via Rimfire Resources.

job.title: Discharge Supervisor
job.description:

Reporting to the Shipping Manager, the Discharge Supervisor will plan, coordinate and oversee bulk fertiliser vessel discharges across eastern Australia. job.description:

The Cotton Research and Development Corporation (CRDC) delivers research, development and extension outcomes for Australia’s cotton industry.   • Strong written communication skills suitable for Board and executive documentation
  • Well-developed interpersonal, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills

job.title: Accountant - Agribusiness
job.description:

To be successful in this position you will have:

  • Experience in commercial accounting, management accounting, commodity accounting or a related finance role.
  • Strong understanding of inventory reconciliation, financial reporting, P&L analysis and management accounting.
  • Exposure to grain, commodity trading, logistics or agribusiness operations would be highly regarded.
  • Strong analytical capability, attention to detail and confidence working with large volumes of financial and operational data.
  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience using ERP systems, commodity trading platforms, Power Query, Power BI or similar reporting tools beneficial.

Why This Role

In return, you will be joining an expanding agribusiness with multiple domestic assets and a growing export operation, in a role that provides broad exposure across trading, finance, risk and operations.
